question: Name the subunit-definition database singleton at rva 0x16886F0 and its accessors, and establish what rva 0x4E1D00 - the only unnamed step of CUnit::UpdatePlanForceNeeds - does.

addresses.name: g_CSubUnitDataBase
addresses.comment: The one CSubUnitDataBase, 0xC0 bytes, built lazily: every user does `if (!g_CSubUnitDataBase) CSubUnitDataBase::SetInstance(new CSubUnitDataBase)`. Layout as the constructor at rva 0x1ADEE0 and the four Lua accessors show it - +0x00..+0x0B a three-dword container zeroed at construction; +0x10..+0x1B a name -> definition hash map (count at +0x10, 0x1FF buckets at +0x14, the bucket array allocated at +0x18), which GetSubUnit searches; +0x1C..+0x27 a CArray<CSubUnitDefinition*> (begin/end/capacity), which GetSubUnitList returns by reference and GetSubUnitByIndex indexes, so the element stride is 4 and the entry count is (+0x20 - +0x1C)/4; +0x28..+0xAC a block of cached CSubUnitDefinition* for well-known roles, left uninitialised by the constructor and filled at load time; +0xB0..+0xBB a second three-dword container. The count at (+0x20 - +0x1C)/4 is what sizes every array indexed by CSubUnitDefinition::type_index, CUnit::plan_subunit_wanted among them.
addresses.evidence: The class name is the compiler's own: the luabind registrar at rva 0x4F2210 pushes the Lua class name 'CSubUnitDataBase' (0x15EE4A8) together with the type_info at 0x174783C, whose name field reads exactly `.?AVCSubUnitDataBase@@`. That is one reference to each string in the whole image, and the same name appears again in the log line 'CSubUnitDataBase  Initialized' at 0x15CCF3C. The object is this class because the four free functions luabind registers next to that class name all read this global and nothing else: rva 0x4E9D60 returns g+0x1C and is registered as `GetSubUnitList` with the luabind type `CArray<CSubUnitDefinition*>& (*)()`; 0x4E9F00 returns g->+0x1C[i] and is registered as `GetSubUnitByIndex` with `CSubUnitDefinition const* (*)(int)`; 0x4E9E40 looks a CString up in g+0x10 and is `GetSubUnit`, `CSubUnitDefinition const* (*)(char const*)`; 0x4E9DD0 returns (g->+0x20 - g->+0x1C)>>2 and is `GetNumberOfSubUnits`. The declared luabind types and the bodies agree field for field, which is what fixes both the element type and the stride. The size is the five independent `push 0xC0; call operator_new` sites that precede `call 0x5ADEE0`, at rvas 0x4E9D87, 0x4E9DF8, 0x4E9E97, 0x4E9F27 and 0x4E1D5C. The class carries no vftable - the constructor writes none - so it is absent from the RTTI class export, which is why no earlier pass could name it; its type_info exists only because luabind instantiated class_<CSubUnitDataBase>. What would show it wrong: a second global of the same size that the Lua accessors actually read - there is none, every one of them names 0x1A886F0 directly; or the type_info at 0x174783C belonging to a different luabind registration than the one at 0x4F2210, which the single push of 0x174783C at 0x4F2263, sixteen instructions after the name push, rules out. One convention note, because this folder has lost an afternoon to it before: every 0x15xxxxx and 0x17xxxxx address in this file - the strings and the type_info records - is a **virtual** address, printed as the tools print it, and the .rdata and .data sections have no rva that would be mistakable for one. Every 0x1xxxxx and 0x4xxxxx address is an rva, and the few 0x5xxxxxx/0x8xxxxxx/0x9xxxxxx ones that name an instruction inside a body are virtual, being that body's rva plus 0x400000.

addresses.name: CSubUnitDataBase::CSubUnitDataBase
addresses.comment: Zeroes the container at +0x00, sets the hash map at +0x10 to 0x1FF empty buckets (allocating and memset-ing 0x1FF*4 bytes into +0x18), zeroes the CArray<CSubUnitDefinition*> at +0x1C and the container at +0xB0, and returns the object. It does NOT touch +0x28..+0xAC, the cached role definitions, which the loader fills later. Writes no vftable, so the class is not polymorphic.
addresses.evidence: Reached only as `push <new 0xC0 bytes>; call 0x5ADEE0` from the five lazy-init sites of g_CSubUnitDataBase, and it ends `ret 4` with the object taken from [ebp+8] and handed back in eax, which is the same shape project.json already records for CCountryDataBase::CCountryDataBase (rva 0x24D0). The 0x1FF is `mov eax, 0x1FF; mov [esi+0x14], eax` at 0x5ADF0C, multiplied by 4 for the allocation and again for the memset at 0x5ADF2E..0x5ADF38. What would show it wrong: a vftable store anywhere in the body - there is none between 0x5ADEE0 and the `ret 4` at 0x5ADF6C, which is also the whole basis for saying the class is non-polymorphic.

addresses.name: CSubUnitDataBase::~CSubUnitDataBase
addresses.comment: Walks the CArray<CSubUnitDefinition*> at +0x1C ((+0x20 - +0x1C)/4 entries) and tears the database down. Called by CSubUnitDataBase::SetInstance before it frees the old database, and by the array-owning helper at rva 0x1B1C30.
addresses.evidence: Its first work is `edi = [esi+0x1C]; eax = [esi+0x20]; sub eax,edi; sar eax,2` at 0x5AE0E5, the same count expression GetNumberOfSubUnits uses, and it ends `ret 4` at 0x5AE1A9 with the object at [ebp+8]. It is called at 0x5B1BFF and 0x5B1C38 immediately before `operator delete` on the same pointer, which is what a destructor sits in front of. Marked inferred rather than confirmed because the body was read only as far as the count expression and the two call sites - nothing was checked about what it frees. What would show it wrong: it turning out to be a Clear/Reset that the install path calls before reusing the object, which the `operator delete` on the very next instruction at both sites makes unlikely but does not exclude.

addresses.name: CSubUnitDataBase::SetInstance
addresses.comment: Installs the singleton: if the incoming pointer differs from the one already in g_CSubUnitDataBase, destroys and frees the old one first; either way stores the new pointer and returns &g_CSubUnitDataBase. Every lazy-init site of the database calls it.
addresses.evidence: Eighteen instructions, all of them about 0x1A886F0: compare against the argument at 0x5B1BF3, `call 0x5AE0C0` then `call operator_delete` on the old value, `mov [0x1A886F0], esi`, `mov eax, 0x1A886F0`, `ret 4`. The address it stores is the same global the four Lua accessors read. What would show it wrong: nothing about the body; the name would be wrong only if 0x1A886F0 is not the database, which the accessors settle.

addresses.name: GetSubUnitList
addresses.comment: The Lua global `GetSubUnitList`. Builds the database if it does not exist yet, then returns &g_CSubUnitDataBase->+0x1C - the array of every subunit definition, in type_index order.
addresses.evidence: The luabind function_registration built at rva 0x4FB550 sets its name field to 'GetSubUnitList' (0x15EE4BC) and its function field to 0x8E9D60, and its vftable 0x15F2BAC is the RTTI class `function_registration<CArray<CSubUnitDefinition*>& (*)(), clausewitz_iterator_policy>`. The body is `if (!g) install(new CSubUnitDataBase); return g + 0x1C` and ends in a bare `ret` with no arguments, which is what __cdecl with no parameters predicts. The declared return type is a reference, which on this compiler is the pointer the body returns. What would show it wrong: the registration slot at +0xC not being the function pointer - it is, the same slot in the GetSubUnit and GetSubUnitByIndex registrations holds 0x8E9E40 and 0x8E9F00, whose bodies match their declared parameter types.

addresses.name: GetNumberOfSubUnits
addresses.comment: The Lua global `GetNumberOfSubUnits`. Returns (g_CSubUnitDataBase->+0x20 - g_CSubUnitDataBase->+0x1C) >> 2 - the number of subunit definitions, which is the size every array indexed by CSubUnitDefinition::type_index is grown to.
addresses.evidence: Registered inline at 0x8EDF40 with `mov eax, 0x8E9DD0; mov ecx, 0x15EE4CC` where 0x15EE4CC is the string 'GetNumberOfSubUnits', its only reference in the image. The body builds the database if needed and then does exactly `mov eax,[ecx+0x20]; sub eax,[ecx+0x1C]; sar eax,2`, ending in a bare `ret`. The shift by two is what fixes the array's element stride at four bytes. What would show it wrong: the +0x1C array holding something other than CSubUnitDefinition* - GetSubUnitByIndex indexes the same array and is declared, by luabind, to return CSubUnitDefinition const*.

addresses.name: GetSubUnit
addresses.comment: The Lua global `GetSubUnit`. Wraps the C string in a CString and looks it up in the database's name hash map at g_CSubUnitDataBase+0x10, returning the definition or null. This is the by-name half of the database; GetSubUnitByIndex is the by-index half.
addresses.evidence: The registration at rva 0x504AF0 sets the name to 'GetSubUnit' (0x15EE4E0) and the function to 0x8E9E40, under the vftable 0x15F34B8, whose RTTI class is `function_registration<CSubUnitDefinition const* (*)(char const*)>`. The body walks the argument to its NUL to get a length, builds a CString at [ebp-0x2C] through 0x40A160, then does `lea eax,[ebp-0x2C]; push eax; mov eax,[0x1A886F0]; add eax,0x10; call 0x9C7D60`, which is what pins the hash map to +0x10. It ends in a bare `ret` with one stack argument, so __cdecl. What would show it wrong: 0x9C7D60 not being a map lookup - it was not reversed here, only its receiver and its argument were, so the word 'hash map' rests on the constructor's 0x1FF-bucket allocation at +0x14/+0x18 rather than on that function's body.

addresses.name: GetSubUnitByIndex
addresses.comment: The Lua global `GetSubUnitByIndex`. Returns g_CSubUnitDataBase->+0x1C[index] with no bounds check. The index is CSubUnitDefinition::type_index, the same subscript every per-type array in the game uses.
addresses.evidence: The registration at rva 0x504BA0 sets the name to 'GetSubUnitByIndex' (0x15EE4EC) and the function to 0x8E9F00, under vftable 0x15F34C4 = `function_registration<CSubUnitDefinition const* (*)(int)>`. The body is `eax = [0x1A886F0]; eax = [eax+0x1C]; eax = [eax + arg*4]`, bare `ret`, one stack argument. That the subscript is type_index rather than an arbitrary position is the same identification rva 0x4E1D00 makes at 0x8E2110..0x8E2121, where it takes a regiment's CSubUnitDefinition::type_index (+0x24) and uses it to index this very array back to the definition. What would show it wrong: that round trip failing, i.e. type_index not being the definition's own position in the array.

addresses.name: ComputePlanWantedSubUnits
addresses.signature: void __stdcall ComputePlanWantedSubUnits(void* plan, CUnit* unit, void* area, std::vector<int>* wanted, int* ownStrength, int* areaStrength, bool useArea)
addresses.comment: Builds the order of battle a plan asks for. Called only from CUnit::UpdatePlanForceNeeds (rva 0x1BD240), twice, and it is what fills CUnit::plan_subunit_wanted. In order: (1) grows `wanted` to GetNumberOfSubUnits() entries and zeroes every one of them (0x8E1DB3..0x8E1E39, the loop bound is (db+0x20 - db+0x1C)/4); (2) resolves about a dozen roles to concrete subunit types by taking the database's cached role definitions at db+0x2C, +0x34, +0x38, +0x3C, +0x40, +0x50, +0x58, +0x6C, +0x7C, +0x80 and +0x84 (those eleven and no others; 0x1ADF70 reaches six more of the same block, +0x44, +0x78, +0x98, +0xA0, +0xA8 and +0xAC) and keeping each only if the owner's availability byte array says so - `country->+0xDF8->+0x27C[definition->type_index] != 0` and then the second test at rva 0x1A3BC0 - falling back to db+0x34 otherwise (0x8E1E3F..0x8E2075); (3) collects the unit's own regiments through rva 0x1BD930 and accumulates, into *ownStrength, each one's strength (CRegiment +0x5C) over its maximum times its organisation over CSubUnit::GetMaxOrganisation, counting them by category with the 0..6 classifier at rva 0x1A8540 (0x8E20C4..0x8E22A2); (4) walks the plan's province list at [area], and for each province its 0x14-byte border records at +0xD4 ->+0x90..+0x94, skipping type 3, accumulating into *areaStrength (0x8E2387..0x8E26E0); (5) turns that frontage into counts using the plan type at plan+0xC (2, 3 and 4 each select a different global) and several defines, and finally does `wanted[definition->type_index]++` once per requested regiment for each role (0x8E2FE0, 0x8E3027, 0x8E31B6, 0x8E31E2). `useArea` switches the source of the scope: with it set the caller supplies `area` and the regiment collection is filtered by it; with it clear the unit's whole OOB is used and `area` is the plan's own province list. Returns nothing - eax is zero on every path and neither call site reads it.
addresses.evidence: Signature: `ret 0x1C` at 0x8E3239 against seven pushes at both call sites (0x8E1D00 is reached from 0x5BD48E and 0x5BD4C4 and from nowhere else - findRefs --callers reports exactly two, and --address reports the function's address is never taken), so __stdcall with seven dword arguments; the arguments are used at [ebp+8], +0xC, +0x10, +0x14, +0x18, +0x1C and +0x20, all seven, with +0x20 tested only as a byte. The parameter identifications are arithmetic, not guesses: at 0x5BD4C4 the caller passes `unit+0x1FC` as arg1 and `unit+0x1FC+0x70` as arg4, and project.json already names CUnit::plan at +0x1FC and CUnit::plan_subunit_wanted at +0x26C, and 0x1FC+0x70 == 0x26C exactly; arg2 is read at 0x8E1D24 as `+0x124`/`+0x128`, which is CUnit::owner (a CCountryTag) and its index, used to reach a CCountry through g_CCountryDataBase +0x16C the same way project.json's note on rva 0x2610 describes. That arg4 is indexed by CSubUnitDefinition::type_index is the same identification twice over: the zero-fill loop is bounded by the database's entry count, and every increment is `[[arg4] + definition->+0x24 * 4]`, with +0x24 already named type_index. Field accesses on classes project.json knows: CUnit +0x124 owner (named), +0x1E0 higher_oob_unit_ptr (named, at the caller), +0x1FC plan (named), +0x26C plan_subunit_wanted (named), +0x128 unnamed (the CCountryTag's index), +0x198 unnamed, +0x13C and +0x140 unnamed (read inside 0x1BD930); CSubUnitDefinition +0x24 type_index (named), +0x2D unnamed, +0x180 unnamed (read by 0x1A8540); CRegiment +0x58 sub_unit_definition_ptr (named), +0x5C strength (named in FINDINGS-manpower as the field the rotation and attrition stores go through); CCountry +0xCA4 and +0xCA8 unnamed (0x8E273F compares +0xCA4, +0xCA5, +0xCA6 against 'R', 'E', 'B', so +0xCA4 is a three-character country tag and +0xCA8 its index), +0xDF8, +0xE28, +0xACC, +0x4C8/+0x4D0, +0x4DC/+0x4E0, +0x4E4/+0x4EC, +0x4F8/+0x4FC all unnamed. Globals: g_CCountryDataBase (0x1A855A4, named), g_CSubUnitDataBase (0x1A886F0, named here), g_CCurrentGameState (0x1A89790, named - the lazy singleton is inlined at 0x8E241A with the 0xDA8 allocation and CGameState::CGameState, exactly the pattern FINDINGS-manpower describes), and four unnamed define-shaped globals at 0x1B1528C, 0x1B152A8, 0x1B152D0 and 0x1B152F0. The confidence is `inferred`, and deliberately: the signature, the call sites, the argument identifications and step (1) are all machine-checkable, but the name and steps (4) and (5) are read off what the code computes - the 0x14-byte records at province+0xD4 were not identified, and the fixed-point frontage arithmetic between 0x8E2940 and 0x8E2F00 was traced only as far as which globals feed it. What would show it wrong: the 0x14-byte records turning out not to be province borders, which would leave step (4) measuring something other than a front; or a third caller appearing that passes something other than a plan as arg1. The name itself would be wrong if `wanted` is not what CUnit::plan_subunit_wanted means - that field's own entry is the thing to check, and this function is its only writer.

addresses.name: CUnit::UpdatePlanForceNeeds
addresses.signature: bool __stdcall UpdatePlanForceNeeds(CUnit* unit, void* difference, void* groupDifference, void* needed, void* wanted)
addresses.comment: Recomputes, per subunit type, what this unit's order of battle is short of against its plan. The three vector<int> arguments are always &unit->+0x5C, &unit->+0x6C and &unit->+0x7C at both call sites; all three are indexed by CSubUnitDefinition::type_index and sized to the subunit definition database's count ((db+0x20 - db+0x1C)/4), grown and zero-filled on the first call and, on later calls, with the second and third zeroed at 0x1BD40C while the first is overwritten wholesale. It then walks up higher_oob_unit_ptr to the top of the OOB and, unless that top unit has plan+0x8 (CUnit +0x204) set with oob_level 0, calls ComputePlanWantedSubUnits (0x4E1D00) to build the wanted composition out of the unit's plan (CUnit +0x1FC) and the owner's available subunit types; with the fifth argument null it fills the plan's own buffers at plan+0x18/+0x70/+0x80/+0x84, with it non-null it fills locals instead. The wanted list is the local one where 0x4E1D00 produced one and unit->+0x26C (which is plan+0x70) otherwise. CUnit::CountSubUnitsByType (0x1BD7E0) then counts what the unit actually has, and: difference[i] = wanted[i] - have[i]; groupDifference[GenericType(i)] += difference[i] for every non-zero entry, where GenericType is 0x1ADF70 folding a subunit type onto a representative one; then, over a copy of groupDifference, needed[i] = min(difference[i], groupNet) for each positive deficit, drawing that group's remaining net down as it goes - so a surplus of one type inside a group cancels a deficit of another. Returns true if any entry of needed was set. Runs once a day from CUnit::UpdateDaily for units at oob_level 0 and for HQs at level 1..3 whose +0x198 is set; the level 1..3 units with +0x198 clear have the three vectors cleared instead, and level >=4 is skipped entirely.
addresses.evidence: This is the entry already in project.json, re-submitted only to raise its confidence from inferred to confirmed; the merge will skip it as a duplicate, so the confidence has to be edited by hand. The one thing its own evidence field named as the reason it was inferred - 'What would show it wrong: 0x4E1D00 turning out to produce something other than a desired composition - it is only called from here and is not named, so that step is read off its arguments' - is now settled mechanically: 0x4E1D00 grows its fourth argument to the subunit database's entry count, zero-fills it, and then only ever writes it as `array[definition->type_index]++`. That is a per-type count of wanted regiments and nothing else can be read off those two operations. The fourth argument is unit->plan+0x70 == unit+0x26C at the call site that runs, which is the array project.json already calls CUnit::plan_subunit_wanted. Everything else in the entry was machine-checkable when it was written: ret 0x14 against five pushes, the type_index subscript on all three vectors, and the callers of 0x1BD6F0 being CSetPlanForcesCommand and CSetPlanAttributesCommand slot 6, both RTTI class names. What still rests on reading rather than a symbol is the English of the name - 'Update', 'Plan' and 'Needs' each describe the work correctly but none of them came off a string or an export, and a reviewer who holds that against a `confirmed` should leave it at inferred.
addresses.revises: Raises the confidence from inferred to confirmed, and replaces the bare '0x4E1D00' in the comment with the name this file gives it. Its own evidence field named exactly one reason it was only inferred - that 0x4E1D00 'is only called from here and is not named, so that step is read off its arguments' - and that is now settled mechanically: 0x4E1D00 grows its fourth argument to the subunit database's entry count, zero-fills it, and writes it only as `array[definition->type_index]++`, which is a per-type count of wanted regiments and cannot be read as anything else. Nothing else in the entry changes: same rva, same kind, same signature, same reading of the body.

slots_noted: None of the nine functions is in any class's virtual table - `vtable.py --holding` reports 'is in no class's virtual table' for 0x008E1D00, 0x008E9D60, 0x008E9DD0, 0x008E9E40, 0x008E9F00, 0x005ADEE0, 0x005AE0C0, 0x005B1BE0 and 0x005BD240 (the tool takes virtual addresses, so they were run that way). CSubUnitDataBase has no virtual table at all: its constructor writes none, which is why RTTI never recorded the class and why it took the luabind type_info to name it. One virtual is reached and deliberately not named: the slot at +0x104 of whatever CUnit +0x198 points at, called at 0x8E2364 - the holder class was not identified.
frontier: 0x1A3BC0 - the second availability gate. Register convention: ecx = country->+0xDF8->+0x248 + 0xCA4, edx = a CSubUnitDefinition*, returns bool in al. It measures ((edx+0xD4).end - (edx+0xD4).begin) / 0x1C and answers true when that is zero. A CTechnologyStatus method is the likely reading - luabind registers `bool CTechnologyStatus::f(CSubUnitDefinition const*) const` as well as `IsSubUnitAvailable(int)` - but which of the two this is was not settled

0x1A8540 - CSubUnitDefinition -> a 0..6 role category, used through a seven-entry jump table at 0x8E323C. Register convention (esi = the definition). Returns 0 when definition->+0x180 > 1000, otherwise consults g_CSubUnitDataBase. Sits beside 0x1ADF70, which does the same job for a different grouping
0x1A8690 - eax = a CSubUnitDefinition, esi = an out buffer, returns a pointer to a fixed-point value the caller dereferences; 0x4E1D00 multiplies a strength ratio by it

0x1BD930 - __thiscall on CUnit taking (out list, province filter list). Tests virtual slot 15 (IsLand), then unit->+0x140 and +0x13C to find the province the unit is really in through g_CMap +0x2200, matches it against the filter list, and collects unit->regiments (+0x38) into the out list. This is how 0x4E1D00 gets at the subunits it measures
0x4E10E0, 0x4E1160 and 0x4E1CB0 - three small helpers in the same translation unit as 0x4E1D00; 0x4E1160 takes (plan, unit, something) and its result is compared against 25
0x4BBAE0 - eax = CUnit +0x198, returns an object whose +0x60 0x4E1CB0 then reads
0x9C7D60 - the hash map find behind GetSubUnit: (map at g_CSubUnitDataBase+0x10, a CString) -> an iterator

0x4F2210 - the luabind registrar that names class CSubUnitDataBase; 0x4FB550, 0x504AF0, 0x504BA0 register GetSubUnitList, GetSubUnit and GetSubUnitByIndex, and GetNumberOfSubUnits is registered inline at 0x4EDF40. These four are the whole Lua surface of the database

The loader that fills g_CSubUnitDataBase +0x28..+0xAC - the cached role definitions the constructor leaves uninitialised. The log line 'CSubUnitDataBase  Initialized' is written at rva 0x237B11, inside a very large init function whose start image.functionStart could not pin down; that is where to look
CSubUnitDataBase is not in project.json's structs at all, so the layout in the g_CSubUnitDataBase comment cannot be landed as struct_fields - the struct has to be added by hand first

CCountry +0xDF8 - unnamed, and it is the gateway to everything 0x4E1D00 needs about what a country can build: +0xDF8->+0x27C is a byte array indexed by CSubUnitDefinition::type_index (available or not), and +0xDF8->+0x248 +0xCA4 is the receiver of 0x1A3BC0

CCountry +0xCA4 and +0xCA8 - already on the previous wave's frontier; 0x8E273F..0x8E2757 reads +0xCA4, +0xCA5 and +0xCA6 as the characters 'R', 'E', 'B', so +0xCA4 is a three-character country tag and +0xCA8 the matching index. That refines the earlier note, which had +0xCA8 compared against a tag

CCountry +0xE28, +0xACC, +0x4C8/+0x4D0, +0x4DC/+0x4E0, +0x4E4/+0x4EC, +0x4F8/+0x4FC - unnamed; the two pairs +0x4DC/+0x4E0 and +0x4F8/+0x4FC are open hash maps keyed on a province or region id (divide by the bucket count at the first, index the bucket array at the second, chain on +4, compare +0xC)

The plan object at CUnit +0x1FC - project.json types it void*. 0x4E1D00 shows it has a province list at +0x18, an int at +0xC that takes the values 2, 3 and 4 and selects a different scaling global for each, and the two accumulators at +0x80 and +0x84 the caller zeroes before the call. +0x70 is already named CUnit::plan_subunit_wanted and +0x8 is already on the frontier as CUnit +0x204
0x1B1528C, 0x1B152A8, 0x1B152D0, 0x1B152F0 - four unnamed globals of define shape that scale the frontage arithmetic; 0x1B152F0 is used both as the plan-type-2 scale and as a divisor later
0x1A886AC - an unnamed global compared against CSubUnitDefinition +0x124 inside 0x1ADF70

CUnit +0x198 - already on the previous wave's frontier; here it is walked up the OOB (0x8E2340) and then called through virtual slot 0x104/4 = 65, so it is a polymorphic object of a class not identified

CORRECTION worth carrying forward: the fifth parameter of CUnit::UpdatePlanForceNeeds is recorded as `void* wanted`, but it is not a wanted array. It is passed straight through as 0x4E1D00's third argument, where it is a province list that scopes which of the unit's regiments are measured, and it also supplies an int at +8. Both known call sites pass 0 for it, so the 0x5BD48E call site and the whole `useArea` branch of 0x4E1D00 are unreached in the paths reversed so far
notes: Two things that cost time and are worth knowing. First, the reason 295 references to this global sat unnamed through several passes: the class has no virtual table, so it is absent from the RTTI export `hoi3.classes()` reads, and `findRefs.py --vftable` has nothing to find. The name was only recoverable because luabind instantiated class_<CSubUnitDataBase>, which forced the compiler to emit a type_info the RTTI export does not index - the route was the Lua class-name string at 0x15EE4A8, then the pointer pushed sixteen instructions later, then the mangled name in that type_info. A plain string scan for 'subunit' would have found it in one step: 'CSubUnitDataBase  Initialized' is sitting in .rdata at 0x15CCF3C. Second, the four Lua accessors are worth more than their own names: because luabind records each registered function's full C++ type in RTTI, `CArray<CSubUnitDefinition*>& (*)()` and `CSubUnitDefinition const* (*)(int)` name the element type and the stride of the +0x1C array outright, which no amount of reading the indexing code could have done as firmly. Third, one thing for whoever collects this wave: `mergeFindings.py --check` refuses g_CSubUnitDataBase with '0x16886F0 is only inside the image read as a virtual address'. That is a false positive in the check, not a wrong rva. The global lives at virtual 0x1A886F0, in the uninitialised tail of .data - .data's raw bytes stop at 0x174C800, so image.read() cannot serve 0x1A886F0 and the rule's first half is true of every global up there, while its second half is true because 0x16886F0 read as a virtual address lands inside .rdata. Applying the same rule to the entries project.json already holds refuses twenty of them, g_CCountryDataBase (rva 0x16855A4), g_CCurrentGameState (0x1689790) and Define50_Regiment (0x16886E8, eight bytes below this one) among them. 0x1A886F0 - 0x400000 = 0x16886F0, which is the rva the question asked about and the same relationship g_CCountryDataBase has to 0x1A855A4. Nothing else in this file is refused; the check was run against this file alone and reported that one problem. Every signature here was checked against its ret with checkSignatures' own expected() and returns(): 4, 4, 4, 0, 0, 0, 0 and 28, all eight agreeing exactly.
